episodes.212677: Very hot temperatures in the mid 90s led to an environment favorable for pulse severe storms as a front dropped into the area.
episodes.212687: A line of thunderstorms tracked east through southern Middle Tennessee during the late afternoon of June 13, 2026. As these thunderstorms crossed the Tennessee River, they produced strong winds, downing a couple trees in the area. The thunderstorms weakened as they moved into a more unfavorable environment east of Interstate 65.
episodes.212698: A few thunderstorms during the late evening hours into early morning across northern section of Eastern NC. A couple storms became severe and produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.212802: Afternoon thunderstorms fueled by abundant low level moisture developed over the high terrain of New Mexico both June 12th and 13th. A large scale area of high pressure stretching back east over the southern CONUS resulted in light steering flow pushing storms eastward through the late day and evening hours. Due to persisting drought conditions, outflow gusts from storms along and west of the Rio Grande Valley resulted in some blowing dust, including an event at the Double Eagle Airport in western Albuquerque June 12th. Elsewhere, severe hail and wind gusts resulted from strong thunderstorms mainly over northeastern NM. There was a report of thunderstorm wind damage near Moriarty where a barn roof was blown off from an estimated 60 mph wind gust.
episodes.212956: A weak surface boundary over the area and the sea breeze led to developing storms in the afternoon in a moderately unstable environment with MLCAPE greater than 1000 J/kg. While coverage of storms was limited, DCAPE greater than 1000 J/kg led to a favorable downburst environment. One storm reached severe limits.
episodes.213080: Scattered thunderstorms moved across portions of northeast Illinois during the late evening of June 13th into the early morning of June 14th, producing isolated wind damage.
episodes.213168: Severe thunderstorms with tornadoes and damaging winds occurred late in the evening of June 13, 2026. Repeated rounds of heavy rainfall caused flash flooding and river flooding. Between 3 and 6 inches of rainfall fell with this system. Some fatalities occurred from the flooding.
episodes.213340: A cold front continued to move through the Mid-Atlantic on Friday, June 12th. This sparked additional clusters of thunderstorms. A few of these storms produced estimated gusts to 70 mph and sporadic hail.
episodes.213353: A cold front continued to move through the Mid-Atlantic on Friday, June 12th. This sparked additional clusters of thunderstorms with localized gale- to storm-force winds.
episodes.213717: Scattered supercells developed and moved into north central Kansas in the late afternoon period. Hazards reported were initially large hail to 2 inches in diameter before the convection formed into a line, tracking southeast during the evening hours. The storms produced winds around 70 mph and heavy rainfall amounts to 3.5 inches.
episodes.213753: Hot conditions prevailed across the Panhandles during the week of June 8 through 12. However, the combination of lingering moisture, a dryline and these hot conditions allowed for a few thunderstorms to develop each day during the afternoon and evening. Some of these storms were severe with hail and damaging winds being the main hazard.
episodes.213758: Hot conditions prevailed across the Panhandles during the week of June 8 through 12. However, the combination of lingering moisture, a dryline and these hot conditions allowed for a few thunderstorms to develop each day during the afternoon and evening. Some of these storms were severe with hail and damaging winds being the main hazard.
episodes.213759: A cold front dropped south into the region and combined with a warm, moist and unstable airmass to bring isolated showers and thunderstorms to the region on the afternoon and evening of June 13. Storms primarily affected the east and northeast Texas Panhandle with damaging winds and small hail.
episodes.213982: Strong to severe thunderstorms developed across portions of northeastern Oklahoma during the late afternoon of the 13th, along a pre-existing outflow boundary from earlier organized thunderstorms that moved through Arkansas. The atmosphere became very unstable during the afternoon across the region, and deep layer wind shear was strong. This combination resulted in several supercell thunderstorms developing, which produced large hail up to two inches in diameter and damaging wind gusts. ||Thunderstorms also developed along a cold front stretching across south central Kansas during the late afternoon and early evening. These thunderstorms moved southeast across northeastern Oklahoma during the evening and organized into a squall line, which produced a number of damaging wind reports.
episodes.213995: An outflow boundary coming from a line of thunderstorms located to the northwest of Eastern North Carolina tracked southeastwards and entered into the Albemarle Sound during the late evening hours of June twelfth. As this occurred, showers and thunderstorms developed and strengthened along this boundary as it continued southeastwards into the morning hours of June thirteenth with a few of these storms becoming strong in nature. This brought strong wind gusts to portions of the Albemarle Sound southeastwards to the Pamlico Sound and coastal waters near Oregon Inlet.
episodes.214000: On June 10th, an inverted trough over the Atlantic Ocean waters adjacent to the northeast Florida and southeast Georgia waters developed coastal showers that moved onshore in the overnight into morning hours. Showers interacted with the land breeze creating a convergent line of heavy showers that caused flooding along the coast. Moist west-southwest flow then developed resulting in typical summertime sea breeze thunderstorms each afternoon into evening for the next several days. The strongest storms were along the sea breeze collisions near HWY 301 and U.S. Route 23.
episodes.214069: A cold front moved slowly southward through the Mid-Atlantic, triggering scattered thunderstorms with heavy rainfall rates and severe weather. While shear was not very high (<30 knots), the atmosphere was considerably unstable with SBCAPE values of at least 2000 J/kg. Low level lapse rates and mid-level lapse rates were up to 8.5 C��/km and  6.5��C/km, respectively, in the Piedmont. All these parameters, combined with DCAPE values of 1000-1400 J/kg, resulted in scattered severe thunderstorms bringing numerous trees down the New River Valley and the Piedmont of Virginia. A gradient of negative omega values (upward motion) across southwest Virginia was noted as the storms passed, likely keeping the storms active in spite of crossing over the Appalachians. This storm episode is notable as gusty winds from the storms' outflow resulted in wind damage in areas that did not meet warning criteria. One was strong enough to knock over a tent in Bedford, killing 1 and injuring 22 at an outdoor event.
episodes.214142: A cold front moved slowly southward through the Mid-Atlantic, triggering scattered thunderstorms with heavy rainfall rates and severe weather. While shear was not very high (<30 knots), the atmosphere was considerably unstable with SBCAPE values of at least 2000 J/kg. Low level lapse rates and mid-level lapse rates were up to 8.5 C��/km and  6.5��C/km, respectively, in the Piedmont. All these parameters, combined with DCAPE values of 1000-1400 J/kg, resulted in scattered severe thunderstorms that reached as far south as North Carolina. One storm in particular sent a swath of trees and power lines down in Mount Airy of Surry County. This storm formed and intensified after crossing the Blue Ridge and shortly dissipated in Stokes County.
episodes.214347: Several rounds of severe thunderstorms impacted northern Oklahoma on the 13th and early morning hours of the 14th. The first featured a slowly decaying line of thunderstorms during the early morning of the 13th, producing a few observations of severe winds and wind damage. Later in the afternoon, a pair of supercell thunderstorms developed along a remnant outflow boundary across the region. Provided strong instability and steep lapse rates, several reports of large hail and damaging wind gusts were received with this activity. Later, a semi-organized convective line (along an approaching cold front) impacted similar areas, leading to additional reports of mainly damaging/severe wind gusts.
episodes.214655: A typical summertime pattern produced scattered afternoon showers and thunderstorms with isolated severe weather reported.
episodes.214657: A jet streak moved though Minnesota on the south edge of a deep mid-level trough. An enhanced low-level jet developed through the Central Plains and extended through eastern Nebraska. With a narrow zone of strong elevated instability from 2000-3000 J/kg and effective shear around 30 knots, scattered elevated storms formed across eastern Nebraska. One storm drifted north into far southern Woodbury County and produced large hail.
episodes.214679: A lifting warm front across Arkansas in cohesion with a subtle, but impactful upper level shortwave trough would lead to multiple reports of severe wind, severe hail, and Flash Flooding across central Arkansas. Additionally, a landspout tornado would occur along the convergence of two outflow boundaries in rural central Arkansas.
episodes.214759: Isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms developed along a quasi-stationary front extending across southern Missouri and northwest Tennessee during the afternoon hours of June 13, 2026.  These storms were supported by SBCAPE values of 3000 to 4000 J/kg and 0-6km bulk shear values of around 30 knots. The storms formed into a line by late afternoon, with several reports of damaging winds. Slow-moving storms combined with precipitable water values around 2 inches to produce heavy rainfall and isolated flash flooding.
episodes.214899: A line of severe storms rapidly developed along an advancing cold front across central Kansas during the evening hours of June 13. At the same time, a left-moving supercell developed in Sumner County and quickly moved northeastward into the Flint Hills. Storms eventually merged and became a large complex of strong to severe storms that moved through south-central and southeast Kansas during the nighttime hours. These storms produced up to 85 mph winds and up to softball size hail.
episodes.215000: Thunderstorms developed during the early morning hours across the central Sandhills. This activity, aided by a low level jet, quickly became severe as it developed and tracked east. Hail up to the size of baseballs was reported near Calamus Reservoir. Storms persisted until around sunrise before dissipating.
episodes.215181: During the evening hours on the 12th, a lone thunderstorm developed across Greeley county, along a warm front approaching from the south. Golfball sized hail was reported before the storm dissipated rapidly as it moved east.
episodes.215311: A couple of thunderstorms moved into the South Carolina foothills from the mountains during mid-evening. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in Greenville County.
episodes.215395: During the morning hours of June 13, 2026, severe thunderstorms tracked through eastern Nebraska and into southwest Iowa, producing hail and damaging wind gusts. The storms were driven by moisture return from a low-level jet impinging on a slowly sagging cold front. Elevated showers and thunderstorms developed over eastern Nebraska prior to sunrise before moving eastward into an environment characterized by sufficient instability and shear to support severe weather. Notable reports included quarter-sized hail (up to 1.00 inch in diameter) in and around the Omaha metro area���including Fremont (Dodge County), Douglas, and Sarpy counties in Nebraska, as well as Mills and Pottawattamie counties in Iowa. Measured wind gusts ranged from 58 to 60 mph, with an estimated wind gust of 70 mph recorded near Valley, Nebraska.
episodes.215396: During the morning hours of June 13, 2026, severe thunderstorms tracked through eastern Nebraska and into southwest Iowa, producing hail and damaging wind gusts. The storms were driven by moisture return from a low-level jet impinging on a slowly sagging cold front. Elevated showers and thunderstorms developed over eastern Nebraska prior to sunrise before moving eastward into an environment characterized by sufficient instability and shear to support severe weather. Notable reports included quarter-sized hail (up to 1.00 inch in diameter) in and around the Omaha metro area���including Fremont (Dodge County), Douglas, and Sarpy counties in Nebraska, as well as Mills and Pottawattamie counties in Iowa. Measured wind gusts ranged from 58 to 60 mph, with an estimated wind gust of 70 mph recorded near Valley, Nebraska.
episodes.215574: Scattered storms developed ahead of a cold front across portions of central and eastern Virginia on June 12. These storms produced damaging winds as they moved east.
episodes.215576: Scattered storms developed ahead of a cold front across portions of the lower Maryland Eastern Shore on June 12. A few of these storms became severe with isolated damaging winds as they moved east.
episodes.215638: Scattered storms developed ahead of a cold front across portions of central and eastern Virginia on June 12. These storms produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay, coastal waters, and the Lower James River.
episodes.215755: A weak mid-level trough sparked isolated storms over western Utah, bringing primarily sub-severe wind gusts and an isolated severe wind gust in Iron county.
episodes.215784: Showers and thunderstorms popped up and developed over a very hot and humid airmass. A few strong to severe thunderstorms were mixed in, producing damaging wind gusts.
episodes.215869: Hot and humid conditions under high pressure along with an afternoon sea breeze circulation shifting inland led to an environment favorable for strong to severe thunderstorms across Southeast South Carolina.
